neighbours.label: the insect life-stage words larva and pupa (pieces ' lar', ' pup' and the 'a' of 'pupa'), as opposed to other stage words (egg, cocoon, nymph, adult) in the same sentences
fire: Inside the soil, the beetle becomes a pupa for several weeks.
Each fly larva feeds on rotting fruit for about a week.
The moth caterpillars pupate under loose bark in autumn.
A young dragonfly larva hunts tadpoles in the pond.
The bee pupa is sealed inside a wax cell by the workers.
Gardeners often find a cutworm larva curled in the soil.
After the last moult, the butterfly pupa hangs from a twig.
The wasp lays one egg, and the larva eats the spider alive.
quiet: Inside the soil, the beetle becomes an adult after several weeks.
Each fly egg hatches on rotting fruit within a day.
The moth caterpillars spin silk under loose bark in autumn.
A young dragonfly nymph hunts tadpoles in the pond.
The bee egg is placed inside a wax cell by the queen.
Gardeners often find a cutworm moth resting on the soil.
After the last moult, the butterfly cocoon hangs from a twig.
The wasp lays one egg, and the adult flies off to find another spider.
